review_reference: UNSIGNED DRAFT: reviewed_by stays empty until the owner signs 0152_catalog_diagnoses.sql at abfecc3571808e4ad29fdf8c1e202f65b3cdf890e9f3106b74bd6ef1bd19f9c9, 0153_clinician_recent_diagnoses.sql at 45faa6a739056cc07426fdb5363b58c7dda1dbcbc096fb6d1769ae746798500b, runtime-grants.sql at 49b378f5771dc4d3d287727f09f750dbf7dd30d37ef1e66e6ba5c510745c3c82 and this declaration. Backend release E integration (staging-novu-ci-20261005 at 95fa1e52, live since 24 November 2026 22:52 UTC with 0001-0151, plus #320 at bf1a4a56, #321 at 0d5c9de9 and #307 at 99c5c816, as merge commits): 0152 ORD-9 first slice, the ICD-11 diagnosis list and its search (#320); 0153 ORD-9 recent diagnoses (#321); no gap. runtime-grants.sql is live release C's file (1c10c2e0..., unchanged by #330) plus #320's 0152 block and then #321's 0153 block, each unchanged; the union is 49b378f5..., as Rahman computed it (#258, 7147424602). #320 carries #319's governed catalogue loader as of d105933d (no migration, no SQL); it is inert without a signed seed: docs/codes/catalog-approvals.json has no approval, no seed file is committed (the migration image's one-name patterns copy none, and drafts never ship), and the deploy tool's catalogue phase runs only for a dispatch that asks for it (catalog_load, default none; a push always none). #307 (ORD-3 batch progress call) changes no SQL. Owner decisions followed: Q124 A (ICD-11 is the search list, typed ICD-10 codes are named back, nothing is loaded until the clinical lead signs), Q141 B (0150 and 0151 were given to the coordinator, so these are 0152 and 0153). Releases after 0001-0151; production's pending set is then exactly the two migrations below. If a release stops after 0152 commits and before 0153, this declaration no longer matches production's pending set and the controller refuses it (UNREVIEWED_PENDING_MIGRATIONS); the fallback declaration in the release PR (0153 and this runtime-grants.sql only) is for that case and needs its own signature.
evidence: On throwaway PostgreSQL 16 clusters with fictional data only. Database suites, on a build owned by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (0001-0153 by the runner, then the role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql), each suite on its own copy, run by the cluster superuser: 125 of 127 pass, among them catalog-diagnoses (0152), clinician-recent-diagnoses (0153), catalog-search, doctors-start-readings and sealed-qa-front-desk-nurse (my-orders passes when run alone; run six at a time its page-time case went over 10 s on a loaded machine, as it does on the live build). schema and records-processing-draft fail, with the same errors on the same build of live 95fa1e52, so not because of 0152 or 0153 (as release C's and 0150/0151's evidence records). Upgrade (services/ehr-api db:test-staging-upgrade): 0001-0151 as the migrator with live release C's runtime-grants.sql (1c10c2e0...), plan 2 pending, dry run of both in one transaction changes nothing, apply, re-run 0 pending, recorded checksums kept, no row-level security or FORCE setting changed; a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql afterwards changes no runtime privilege (2,854 compared), so the migrations grant exactly what the file grants. On a fresh 0001-0151 build by live 95fa1e52's own runner and bootstrap: plan 2 pending, dry run rolled back (152 recorded), apply (0152 53 ms, 0153 14 ms), a second apply 0 pending. scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs with HID_REHEARSAL_LIVE_TREE = git archive of live 95fa1e52 (live schema 0151): all 12 live runtime verifiers pass after 0152 and after 0153 (the runner can stop between the two); 154 applied, re-run 0 pending, dry run rolled back, the dry run on the live base with a reader in flight passes with nothing applied, and this branch's verifiers (order routes, records processing, own-work patient cards, prescription details, own facility work and the identity ones) pass. It ran on a shared machine with a load average near 20 on 4 cores, where the order-routes verifier took about 170 s, so the passing run raised only the rehearsal's own 180 s per-command limit to 1,200 s in a scratch copy; two unchanged runs stopped at that limit in that verifier, after every check before it had passed. Rahman's note on #330's evidence (#258, 7147424602), recorded here: the rehearsal's cluster has no QA tenant, so 0151 writes nothing there; with the QA tenant installed, 11 of the 12 live verifiers pass at every point, and the 12th, provider enrollment, fails the same way before 0150, because the tenant installs themselves add organization applications; that failure is not 0150-0153's. A stop after 0152 commits was reproduced: after the dry run of 0152-0153 succeeded, the apply printed "Applied 0152_catalog_diagnoses.sql" and stopped on 0153 (a concurrent session held an uncommitted table of 0153's name past the runner's 5 s lock_timeout); the plan then showed 1 pending (0153). The real controller (schema_contract and ECS.migrate with the deploy tests' AWS fakes and that plan) refuses this declaration with UNREVIEWED_PENDING_MIGRATIONS after the plan task only, whether re-sent or carried by a later push, and applies the fallback declaration (0153 and this runtime-grants.sql) when it is pushed alone; the runner then applied 0153, 0 pending. On that database release C's runtime-grants.sql re-run by its bootstrap removes hid_ehr_runtime's EXECUTE on ehr.search_catalog_diagnoses; this file fails while 0153 is pending (ehr.record_recent_diagnosis does not exist) and the bootstrap rolls back. 0152 takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.catalog_versions and ACCESS SHARE on 0149's two lists, NOWAIT, retried every 100 ms for at most 5 s (one attempt inside a dry run that holds other locks), with busy refusals the runner's dry run retries (#306); it pins 0149's status and query helper by md5, owner and search_path. 0153 locks only its new objects (no foreign key) and requires the table and functions to belong to the owner of ehr.catalog_versions. Old images on this schema: live ehr-api calls nothing 0152 or 0153 adds; 0152 replaces ehr.catalog_status() with the same columns and a diagnosis row, which live ehr-api would read as a lab-test row only once an ICD-11 release is active, and none is (nothing is loaded until the clinical lead signs); the new ehr-api answers 503 CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE for the diagnosis search on a schema without 0152 and saves a diagnosis without its recent record on a schema without 0153 (42883 rolled back to a savepoint), so either image may go first or be rolled back alone. So an ICD-11 release is activated only once #320's ehr-api is live (#320's release plan). Release tests 126/126; verify-migration-ledger accepts 0153 (154 files); ehr-api tsc clean and jest 1,973 passed (20 skipped), lab-api 667, pharmacy-api 498; scripts/tests 82 and 1 skipped; deploy tool 79; db:test-runner 15; build gates 70; staging Python 68.
